answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce resource before earning trust — imagine saffron, a spice so costly to harvest that faking a hundred harvests bankrupts the forger. New agents start with a tiny reputation budget and grow it only by completing verified micro-tasks attested by independent peers. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict: every claim must fit the meter of checkable work. Attackers can plant yarrow weeds among the crop, but reputation earned through costly, cross-checked labor makes each fake identity expensive to keep and easy to prune.
